positive.prompt: Write a spec for the new billing feature before we write any code
Draft a PRD with objectives and boundaries for this project
We are starting a new service, define the requirements first
This one requirement covers identity, billing, notifications, and reporting — decompose it into independently specifiable modules first
Before we spec this platform, map the capabilities and their dependency order

negative.prompt: Trace this request across our services
Simplify this clever one-liner into readable code
Break the approved spec into ordered implementation tasks

evals.prompt: We want usage-based billing. Produce the spec before any implementation.
evals.expected_output: A SPEC.md covering objectives, behavior, data model, testing strategy, and explicit boundaries
expectations: The spec includes explicit boundaries and non-goals
Ambiguities are surfaced as questions rather than silently resolved
A testing strategy is part of the spec

evals.prompt: Read portal-brief.md and produce the spec work for the customer portal initiative.
evals.expected_output: A capability map with stable module ids and one-way dependency direction, gated on approval before per-module specs; any module spec written is scoped to its module only
expectations: A capability map with module ids and their dependencies is proposed before any full spec is written
Dependency direction is one-way (no cycles) and drives the proposed build order
Approval of the map is requested before per-module specs are drafted
Any module spec produced is scoped to a single module rather than restating the whole initiative

evals.prompt: Read brief.md and write the architecture-first specification for account document exports. Evaluate the proposed senior patterns before choosing the design. Do not implement.
evals.expected_output: A stack-neutral specification selecting architecture from documented constraints, comparing alternatives and defining export ownership, lifecycle failures and evidence.
expectations: The design compares appropriate alternatives and does not select microservices, CQRS or event sourcing solely because they are called senior patterns
Existing application and worker capabilities are considered without inventing a language, hosting platform or independent deployment requirement
The specification covers account authorization at request and download time, revocation, duplicate job delivery, worker interruption and expiration
Unknown peak load and product decisions are identified; the local rendering observation is not represented as a production guarantee
The document includes ownership, data flow, architecture rationale, reconsideration triggers and a verification strategy
No implementation code is written and unexecuted verification commands are not claimed to have passed
